toc.title: Intel 80386 — What MS-DOS PC Software Relies On
toc.description: Registers, real, protected and VM86 modes, segmentation, paging, exceptions and the IDT

toc.title: Intel x87 FPU — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: Which models have an 80387, 487SX or integrated FPU, the register stack and tags, control and status words, exceptions and CR0 NE/MP/EM/TS/ET, #NM, #MF and the IRQ13 path with ports F0h and F1h, FPU detection, FSAVE/FSTENV images, instruction groups and precision, timing, with the MCP tools and trace filters that show it

toc.title: Pentium on a 430FX PCI Board — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The Pentium 75 to 200 models, CPUID, CR4, RDTSC and the MSRs, the U/V pairing timing, PCI configuration mechanism #1 on the 430FX and PIIX (PAM shadowing, DRAM, PIRQ, ELCR, CF9h, IDE timing), the PCI GD5446 and the SeaBIOS PCI image, with the MCP tools and trace filters that show them

toc.title: PC/AT Board — Memory, I/O, Interrupts, Timers, BIOS and CMOS
toc.description: Models, memory map, A20, board I/O ports and the shadow register, the 8259A pair and IRQ vectors, the 8254, reset paths, the built-in SeaBIOS, firmware config, debug console and the MC146818 CMOS

toc.title: BIOS and DOS Services — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The IVT, BIOS data area and EBDA, the BIOS, DOS, XMS, EMS, DPMI and mouse interrupts and which built-in software provides them, the PSP, environment, MCB chain and EXEC layout, the memory managers and extenders the built-in disks configure, GDXIDLE, GDXRUN, the boot order and BIOS log, and the MCP breakpoints, trace filters and memory reads that find a game's calls

toc.title: CGA, EGA, VGA and the Cirrus Logic Cards — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The six video cards and Auto, the VGA ports and modes, the CL-GD5428 on the ISA and VL-Bus (unlock, banking, the linear aperture, clocks and the hidden DAC), the CGA and its composite output, the write-only EGA, the VBE BIOS, and the debugger and MCP tools that show them

toc.title: Mouse, Joystick, Serial and Parallel Ports — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The PS/2 and serial mouse, the game port and its joysticks, the two 16550A COM ports and LPT1, with the MCP tools and trace filters that drive and watch them

toc.title: IDE and the ATAPI CD-ROM Drive — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The two IDE channels and their positions, the ATAPI CD-ROM drive: signature, IDENTIFY PACKET, the packet protocol and commands, sense codes, tray and disc, CD audio and timing, with the MCP tools and trace filters that drive and watch it

toc.title: Sound Cards, FM, MIDI and the PC Speaker — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The AdLib and Sound Blaster cards with their ports, IRQ and DMA and BLASTER, the OPL2 and OPL3 FM chips (registers, rhythm, 4-op, timers, detection), the DSP (reset, commands, single-cycle, auto-init and high-speed DMA), the SB Pro and SB16 mixers, CD audio level, the MPU-401 UART and the PC speaker, with the MCP tools and trace filters that drive and watch them

toc.title: Floppy Controller and DMA — What MS-DOS Software Relies On
toc.description: The 82077 floppy controller (ports, DOR, MSR, commands, ST0-ST3, IRQ 6 and DMA channel 2, drive types and data rates, disk change, write protect, timing, image formats and geometry detection) and the two 8237A DMA controllers (registers, flip-flop, modes, auto-init, cascade, page registers, 64 KB and 128 KB boundaries, channel assignments), with the MCP tools and trace filters that drive and watch them
